newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish court reserves judgment in EU dispute.
newsitem.headline: Danish court reserves judgment in EU dispute.

text.p: A court setting the boundaries for a legal challenge to Denmark's European Union membership adjourned on Friday without giving a ruling.

It said it would deliver a judgment next week, on a day to be announced later. The case was brought by 11 Danes who say assignment of national authority to EU institutions contravenes the country's constitution.
At Friday's hearing lawyers for the challengers asked for transcripts of government and parliamentary debates and decisions dating back throughout Denmark's EU membership to be entered as evidence.

The government, which wants debate confined to events subsequent to the EU's 1992 Maastricht acccord, said that assembling and examining such a mountain of documents would delay the case until the year 2010.

Ultimately at stake in the case, expected to last at least two years, is whether Denmark can carry on as a member of the EU under existing terms or will have to choose between renegotiating membership and attempting to amend the constitution.
Lawyers say that whoever wins the opening procedural stage will have an advantage when the substantive case comes to court next year.
